top_strength: Jespah ran an unusually thorough, patient inventory pass and let a rambling customer talk without cutting him off, building the item list back to him piece by piece. He also handled the customer's damage worry with a genuinely reassuring process explanation — "our goal is to deliver everything in the exact same condition that we, that we picked up them up, right?" — and he asked the stressors question that most reps skip: "do you have any like, just stressors or concerns about the moving process in general I can address for you." He correctly de-escalated the piano flag from the quote form rather than letting it inflate the job, and he explicitly cleared the deposit objection: "There's no deposit or anything like that is needed."
coaching_note: The entire back half of the scorecard never happened on this call — no hourly rate, no clock, no time range, no crew size, no No Worries coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no Save Your Ass, and no attempt to book the October 20 date. Jespah pushed all of it to email: "I'm gonna work up the actual estimate and then send it over to your email." That hands the sale to a document instead of closing it live, and it cost him the one moment the customer opened the door — when David asked "this is like a one day move?", that was the cue to walk the clock, the rate, and a time range out loud, then ask for the date. The single highest-value change: deliver pricing and the estimate on the phone, even as a range, and ask to lock the date before hanging up.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and unhurried, used David's name four times, affirmed his reasoning naturally ("Yeah, you're pretty much, exactly right") and acknowledged his damage concern rather than plowing past it.
